messages:
olivia: QA found an ugly edge case in the quantization guide. The Python example for 8-bit calibration casts inputs to torch.float32 right before calibration and that breaks on some CUDA/toolchain combos.

raj: ouch. can you paste the snippet or point me to the file/line?

olivia: pasted from the page: 

```python
# quant profile minimal example
model.half()
inputs = inputs.to(torch.float32)
# run calibration...
```

That .to(torch.float32) forces compute back to fp32 which defeats the point for 8-bit flows and causes failures in newer stacks.

sam: :eyes: iirc we meant .to(torch.float16) or not to cast at all. also the SDK example under examples/opt uses redwood.optimize but still assumes fp32 tensors, so we have a dtype mismatch between docs and SDK snippets.

mike: reassigning to @raj to reconcile docs + SDK examples. can we add a tiny smoke test in docs CI that validates dtype consistency?

raj: plan: 1) change the public example to show two patterns: an explicit float16 calibration snippet and a defensive pattern that reads model dtype from parameters; 2) update SDK sample to derive dtype from model; 3) add a small docs-examples unit that runs the snippet across torch matrix and asserts model and input dtypes align; 4) open PR and ping this thread.

olivia: prefer showing explicit short example first (clear for readers) then the defensive pattern. QA wants a short note under "Quantization caveats" listing common gotchas (dtype casts, device pinned RNGs, CLI flags forcing fp32).

raj: updated snippet locally. defensive pattern looks like: 

```python
from redwood import optimize
# explicit pattern (fastpath)
model.half()
inputs = inputs.to(torch.float16)
# ...calibrate and quantize...

# defensive pattern
model_dtype = next(model.parameters()).dtype
inputs = inputs.to(model_dtype)
```

sam: nice. make sure code blocks use python3 tag and include minimal imports at top — our example linter flags missing imports. also please avoid wording like "defeats the point" in final copy; use "negates quant benefits" for tone.

raj: opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5110 — added both snippets, the caveats blurb, and a short smoke test under docs-examples/tests/test_quant_dtype.py. pinged @docs-bot to run CI.

docs-bot: build queued for branch raj/quant-dtype-fix (docs-ci)

mike: when you update the SDK example, add a tiny requirements.txt entry for the docs-examples job so the CI matrix can install the correct torch versions. also leave a short backward-compat note for v2 docs.

raj: will add requirements and a matrix entry for torch==2.2, torch==2.3, and nightly. tests will only run the dtype assert; keeping them tiny.

qa: once CI shows green we'll re-run the regression that initially triggered this. it's blocking a minor release if customers hit it.

raj: pushed fixes and tests. initial CI failed due to unrelated samplegen flake; fixed and re-ran. build now: queued.

docs-bot: build succeeded for raj/quant-dtype-fix (docs-ci)

qa: re-ran the real repro case against the patched example — PASS. documentation smoke looks good.

mike: please open a backport PR to the v2-docs repo after this merges. add a one-sentence release-note blurb in the PR description.

raj: adding checklist in PR: changelog entry, tests, QA signoff, backport PR created. will also add a cross-link on the Optimize toolkit overview so users searching "quant profile" hit the caveats note.

sam: small copy nit: reworded the caveats line to say "negates quant benefits" instead of the original phrasing. also added a short example of CLI flags that force fp32.

olivia: thanks for the quick turnaround everyone. great catch. :tada:

mike: scheduling a tiny release note and a customer-facing advisory in case any active users saw the same issue. @support to monitor tickets and escalate to me if needed.

sam: closing the loop here. tag me if customers hit similar problems and i'll help triage.

olivia: thanks all.
